architecture.rationale: Candidate focus selection is isolated in a deterministic module and integrated into the executor.

autonomy.rationale: The system can preserve an active monetization mission without repeated owner intervention, while external claims remain evidence-gated.

initiative.rationale: Approved and already-started work now takes precedence over newly discovered candidates, reducing passive candidate churn.

results.rationale: The change redirects effort toward completing one deliverable and obtaining one external receipt, but no verified submission or revenue exists yet.

robustness.rationale: Deterministic regression tests cover active locks, approval preference, fallback selection and abandonment release.

safety.rationale: The change does not weaken external action guardrails and prevents accidental work switching from being mistaken for progress.

memory.rationale: Execution receipts become durable focus memory across autonomous cycles.

validations.capability: An active execution receipt prevents a newly ranked candidate from replacing unfinished paid work.
An explicitly approved executable candidate is selected ahead of an unapproved higher-ranked candidate.
